file.description: Minimal broker implementation for market orders only. No shorting allowed (must have cash to buy, must have shares to sell). Optional slippage and commission simulation.

signal.name: orderAccepted
signal.description: Emitted when order passes validation and is submitted

signal.name: omsError
signal.description: Emitted on order rejection or execution error

method.name: __init__
method.description: Initialize broker with account and price lookup function. Load positions and compute initial portfolio state.

method.name: submit_market_order
method.signature: submit_market_order(ticker: str, side: Literal["BUY", "SELL"], qty: int) -> None
method.description: Validate and submit market order. Synchronously execute against mark_price_fn. Update positions, cash, and emit signals.
method.validation: - qty > 0 - BUY: require cash >= qty * mark_price * (1 + slippage) - SELL: require position.qty >= qty
method.execution: 1. Insert order with status="ACCEPTED" 2. Get fill price from mark_price_fn(ticker) + slippage 3. Apply commission if enabled 4. Insert fill record 5. Update position (FIFO average cost via portfolio.apply_fill) 6. Insert ledger entry 7. Update order status="FILLED" 8. Emit signals: orderAccepted, orderFilled, positionsUpdated, portfolioUpdated

method.name: refresh_portfolio
method.description: Revalue all positions using current mark prices. Compute unrealized P&L and equity. Emit portfolioUpdated signal.

method.name: get_position
method.description: Return current position for ticker or None

method.name: get_buying_power
method.description: Return available cash for new buys

file.implementation_notes: - All operations synchronous (executed immediately on GUI thread) - For production: move execution to worker thread - Slippage: if config.ENABLE_SLIPPAGE, fill_price = mark * (1 + random.uniform(-config.SLIPPAGE_BPS, config.SLIPPAGE_BPS) / 10000) - Commission: fee = max(qty * config.COMMISSION_PER_SHARE, config.MIN_COMMISSION) if config.ENABLE_COMMISSION - No partial fills in Phase 2 - No limit/stop orders in Phase 2

file.description: Pure functions for FIFO cost basis tracking and P&L computation. No database or GUI dependencies.

function.name: apply_fill
function.signature: apply_fill(account: Account, position_map: Dict[str, Position], fill: Fill) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Position], float, float]
function.description: Apply fill to position map using FIFO cost basis. BUY: Increase qty, update weighted average cost SELL: Decrease qty, compute realized P&L
function.algorithm:
BUY: new_qty = old_qty + fill.qty new_avg_cost = (old_qty * old_avg_cost + fill.qty * fill.price) / new_qty cash_delta = -(fill.qty * fill.price + fill.fee) realized_pnl = -fill.fee
SELL: new_qty = old_qty - fill.qty cash_delta = fill.qty * fill.price - fill.fee realized_pnl = fill.qty * (fill.price - position.avg_cost) - fill.fee new_avg_cost = position.avg_cost (unchanged)
If new_qty == 0, remove from position_map

function.name: revalue
function.signature: revalue(positions: List[Position], mark_price_fn: Callable[[str], float]) -> Tuple[float, float]
function.description: Compute unrealized P&L for all positions using current mark prices. unrealized_pnl = sum((mark_price - avg_cost) * qty for each position) market_value = sum(mark_price * qty for each position)

file.implementation_notes: - All functions pure (no side effects) - Use Decimal for precise monetary calculations (optional but recommended) - Positions with qty=0 should be removed from position_map

file.purpose: Machine learning for order flow regime detection and forecasting
file.description: Compute features from trade/quote data, cluster into regimes (buyer/balanced/seller), and forecast next-window regime probabilities. Cache results in Supabase.

function.name: compute_features
function.signature: compute_features(ticker: str, window: str, trades: pd.DataFrame, quotes: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame
function.returns: DataFrame with columns: [window_start, window_end, pct_ask, pct_bid, avg_spread, avg_trade_size, volatility, volume_zscore]
function.description: Split trades/quotes into windows (1D/1W/1M/3M/1Y), compute features per window.

feature.name: pct_ask
feature.classification: Trade is "on ask" if trade.price >= quote.ask (within time window) Trade is "on bid" if trade.price <= quote.bid Else: midpoint (not ask or bid)

feature.name: volatility
feature.formula: std(log(price[t] / price[t-1])) * sqrt(252) for daily windows, annualized

feature.name: volume_zscore
feature.description: Z-score of volume relative to past N windows

function.implementation: - Merge trades and quotes on timestamp (as-of join) - Group by window boundaries - Compute features per group - Handle missing data: forward-fill quotes, drop windows with insufficient data

function.name: cluster_regimes
function.description: Apply KMeans clustering (k=3) to features. Clusters represent: buyer-dominant (high pct_ask), balanced, seller-dominant (high pct_bid).
function.algorithm: 1. Normalize features (StandardScaler) 2. KMeans(n_clusters=config.ML_KMEANS_CLUSTERS, random_state=42) 3. Fit on features_df 4. Return labels and centroids
function.cluster_interpretation: Cluster 0: Buyer-dominant (high pct_ask, low pct_bid) Cluster 1: Balanced (mid pct_ask, mid pct_bid) Cluster 2: Seller-dominant (low pct_ask, high pct_bid) (Actual assignment may vary; inspect centroids to determine)

function.name: forecast_next_window
function.description: Train supervised model on historical cluster sequences to predict next window's regime. Use LogisticRegression or RandomForestClassifier.
function.algorithm: 1. Create lag features: cluster_id[t-1], cluster_id[t-2], ... 2. Target: cluster_id[t] 3. Split train/test (last 20% for validation) 4. Train LogisticRegression (multi-class) 5. Predict probabilities for next window (using most recent lags) 6. Return probability distribution

function.name: analyze_or_load_cached
function.description: High-level function: check Supabase cache, fetch if fresh enough, else recompute.
function.algorithm: 1. For each window in windows: a. Query ml_regimes for ticker/window (last 30 days) b. If cached data is recent (computed_at within 24 hours), use cache c. Else: fetch trade/quote data from Polygon.io, compute features, cluster, forecast d. Upsert new regimes and forecast to Supabase 2. Return combined results
function.cache_policy: - Regime data: cache valid for 24 hours - Forecast data: cache valid for 24 hours - If config.ML_CACHE_ENABLED == False, always recompute

file.purpose: Time & Sales tape (trade tape) widget for Info tab
file.description: Displays today's trades in a scrollable table. Backfills on ticker load, appends live trades from WebSocket. Daily rollover when first trade of new day arrives.

layout.table: QTableWidget with columns: Time | Price | Size | Exchange

method.name: loadTicker
method.description: Clear table, fetch today's trades via Polygon.io, populate table. Store current_tape_date (ET date of today).
method.algorithm: 1. Clear table (setRowCount(0)) 2. Get today's ET date (use _get_et_date helper) 3. Fetch trades: polygon_client.fetch_trades_today(ticker) 4. Populate table with trade rows (most recent at bottom) 5. Set current_tape_date = today's ET date 6. Scroll to bottom if auto-scroll enabled

method.name: appendTrade
method.description: Append single trade to table. Check for daily rollover.
method.algorithm: 1. Parse trade timestamp to ET date 2. If ET date > current_tape_date: - Clear table - Set current_tape_date = new ET date - Backfill today's trades (call loadTicker) 3. Else: - Append row to table - Format: time (HH:MM:SS ET), price ($X.XX), size (X,XXX), exchange (code) - Auto-scroll to bottom if enabled and scrollbar at bottom 4. If table rowCount > config.TAPE_MAX_ROWS: - Remove oldest rows (keep most recent TAPE_MAX_ROWS)

method.name: clear
method.description: Clear all rows and reset current_tape_date

function.name: _get_et_date
function.description: Convert UTC datetime to ET date (handle DST)

function.name: _is_at_bottom
function.description: Check if table scrollbar is at bottom position

file.implementation_notes: - Use QTableWidget with 4 columns - Trade time formatted as HH:MM:SS (ET, 24-hour) - Price formatted as $X.XX (2 decimals) - Size formatted with thousand separators (e.g., 1,500) - Exchange: 1-char code (e.g., "Q" for Nasdaq) - Auto-scroll: only scroll if user is already at bottom (don't interrupt manual scrolling) - Backfill uses /v3/trades/{ticker}?timestamp.gte={today_start_ms}&limit=1000 - Daily rollover: detect when trade.timestamp (ET) > current_tape_date

patch.instructions: Add new methods to PolygonClient class for fetching historical trades and quotes. These are used by Time & Sales tape and ML module.

append_to_class.name: PolygonClient
append_to_class.code:
def fetch_trades_today(self, ticker: str) -> List[dict]: """ Fetch all trades for ticker from today's ET market open until now.
Returns list of trade dicts with keys: timestamp, price, size, exchange """ try: # Get today's date in ET et_now = datetime.now(pytz.timezone('America/New_York')) et_today = et_now.date()
# Market open: 9:30 AM ET market_open = datetime.combine(et_today, datetime.min.time().replace(hour=9, minute=30)) market_open = pytz.timezone('America/New_York').localize(market_open)
# Convert to milliseconds timestamp start_ms = int(market_open.timestamp() * 1000)
# Fetch trades url = f"https://api.polygon.io/v3/trades/{ticker}" params = { "timestamp.gte": start_ms, "limit": 1000, "sort": "timestamp", "order": "asc" }
response = self.client.get(url, params=params) response.raise_for_status() data = response.json()
trades = [] for t in data.get("results", []): trades.append({ "timestamp": t.get("sip_timestamp"), # nanoseconds "price": t.get("price"), "size": t.get("size"), "exchange": t.get("exchange", ""), })
return trades
except Exception as e: logging.error(f"Error fetching today's trades for {ticker}: {e}") return []
def fetch_quotes_range(self, ticker: str, start_dt: datetime, end_dt: datetime) -> List[dict]: """ Fetch quote data for ticker in specified datetime range.
Returns list of quote dicts with keys: timestamp, bid, ask, bid_size, ask_size """ try: start_ms = int(start_dt.timestamp() * 1000) end_ms = int(end_dt.timestamp() * 1000)
url = f"https://api.polygon.io/v3/quotes/{ticker}" params = { "timestamp.gte": start_ms, "timestamp.lte": end_ms, "limit": 5000, "sort": "timestamp", "order": "asc" }
response = self.client.get(url, params=params) response.raise_for_status() data = response.json()
quotes = [] for q in data.get("results", []): quotes.append({ "timestamp": q.get("sip_timestamp"), # nanoseconds "bid": q.get("bid_price"), "ask": q.get("ask_price"), "bid_size": q.get("bid_size"), "ask_size": q.get("ask_size"), })
return quotes
except Exception as e: logging.error(f"Error fetching quotes for {ticker}: {e}") return []

known_limitations.limitation: Only market orders supported (no limit/stop orders)
No shorting (must own shares to sell)
Slippage and commission are optional and simplified
ML analysis runs synchronously (may block UI briefly)
Time & Sales tape limited to today's trades (no multi-day history)
Single account per user (no account switching UI)
Delayed data (~15 minutes) for all market data
